column1: # The published reference corpus: a THIRD sample, of Java repositories that state a licence, are still being
# worked on, and publish an artefact. Drawn to compare against reference-corpus.tsv and
# WHY A THIRD SAMPLE. The first two are drawn and neither denominator resembles what this reading is measured
# on. Uniform over GitHub's Java gives coursework: ten of ten with zero stars and no licence. A fifty-star
# floor gives Android: five of ten, plus two pieces of teaching material. The nine evaluation-set members are
# none of those things — they are licensed libraries and servers that publish artefacts and are still
# maintained. A denominator is meant to say what the code being read is written in, so the third frame states
# those three properties directly instead of hoping a popularity proxy reaches them.
# THE FRAME AND THE PREDICATE, both fixed before a single rank was drawn.
#     language:Java fork:false mirror:false size:>=1000 pushed:>=2025-01-01 created:<2026-08-21
#     license:<each of the thirteen GitHub states>
#   `pushed` HAS NO UPPER BOUND, AND BOUNDING IT WAS TRIED AND REVERTED. The frame is not a fixed
#   population: a repository whose last push was in 2024 joins the moment somebody pushes to it, so the
#   count grows. It read 112,183 on 2026-08-20 and 112,251 three days later. Bounding `pushed` above at the
#   same ceiling `created` has was tried, on the reasoning that a fixed population is what makes a draw
#   reproducible. IT IS WORSE, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO.
#     - THE BOUNDED FRAME SHRINKS, AND IT EXPELS THE REPOSITORIES IT ALREADY DREW. `pushed` is a mutable
#       property. Under the upper bound a repository LEAVES the frame the moment anybody pushes to it, so
#       membership falls every day and a row already drawn can stop being a member. Under no upper bound
#       membership only ever grows: a repository pushed since 2025-01-01 stays in however often it is
#       pushed again, so a drawn row is a member forever. Monotone membership is the property that matters.
#     - IT COST 4,959 REPOSITORIES, AND THEY WERE THE MAINTAINED ONES. The bounded frame counted 107,224,
#       against 112,183 for the SAME window three days earlier. Those 4,959 were pushed in between, which
#       is what expelled them — so the bound removes exactly the actively maintained projects, which are
#       the ones that publish an artefact.
#     - THE TAKE RATE COLLAPSED, MEASURABLY. Sixteen ranks under the bounded frame took 3 and rejected 13,
#       against 30 taken of 53 recorded. Under the recorded rate a run of 16 takes 3 or fewer with
#       probability 0.0023, so this is the bound biasing the frame and not sampling noise.
#   NO `pushed` FRAME IS FIXED, BECAUSE `pushed` IS MUTABLE. Reproducibility does not come from re-running
#   the query, and cannot: it comes from THIS FILE, which pins every drawn repository at a commit. A draw is
#   a snapshot, its count is recorded beside it, and `-Dcs.draw.total` states which snapshot a run means to
#   reproduce rather than pretending the population stood still.
#   Each qualifier, and why it is there:
#     language:Java     the population, as GitHub states a primary language
#     fork:false        a fork is another repository's words copied; counting them twice is a sampling defect
#     size:>=1000       one megabyte. A STATED bound, not a derived one, carried over from the first frame
#     pushed:>=2025-01-01   "modern" read as STILL BEING WORKED ON rather than recently started, with no
#                       upper bound so that membership only ever grows and a drawn row stays a member. A library
#                       begun in 2014 and pushed to this year writes today's Java; one begun in 2024 and
#                       abandoned does not. Creation date measures the wrong thing, so `pushed` is used.
#     license:...       the thirteen licences GITHUB ITSELF publishes at /licenses — agpl-3.0, apache-2.0,
#                       bsd-2-clause, bsd-3-clause, bsl-1.0, cc0-1.0, epl-2.0, gpl-2.0, gpl-3.0, lgpl-2.1,
#                       mit, mpl-2.0, unlicense. THE SET IS CITED, NOT CHOSEN: picking which licences count
#                       would be this project curating, so GitHub's own enumeration is used whole. They OR
#                       together in a query, which is what makes "states a licence GitHub recognises"
#                       expressible at all. A licence says nothing about what words a repository contains,
#                       so requiring one does not breach the rule this corpus exists to enforce. IT IS NOT
#                       NEUTRAL — a licensed repository is a more deliberate one — and that is stated rather
#     created:<...      a ceiling, so the frame is the same set on a later day
#   NOT in the frame: stars, watchers, archived state, and anything about subject matter.
#   PREDICATE, applied to every drawn rank without exception. GitHub's repository search cannot ask whether a
#   repository publishes anything, so it is asked of the tree directly, AT THE PINNED COMMIT:
#     accept if pom.xml at the repository root states a <groupId>
#          or if build.gradle or build.gradle.kts at the root applies maven-publish
#     reject otherwise, and take the next rank from the same seeded stream
#   A Maven groupId is the coordinate an artefact publishes under, and maven-publish is the plugin that
#   publishes one, so between them they are what a repository does to make its code available as a library.
#   The predicate is read over raw.githubusercontent.com rather than the API, which is why it costs no rate
#   limit. EVERY REJECTION IS RECORDED with the rank and the reason, in docs/reference-corpus/draw-published.json.
#   Rejection sampling on a predicate stated in advance is uniform over the sub-population that satisfies it.
#   That is the whole reason the predicate had to be written down before the draw ran rather than after: a
#   predicate adjusted once its rejections are visible is a choice about which repositories end up here.
# HOW MANY, and why it is a hundred rather than ten or thirty. The first two samples hold ten each, which is
#   what the plan asked for and is too few. A reference is a pooled density per word, so with ten roughly
#   equal repositories any one of them carries about a tenth of the total mass: a single blockchain
#   repository in the pool would have the reference claim `transaction` is written at a tenth of a blockchain
#   repository's rate, which is enough to demote it for besu. That is the contamination risk the plan names,
#   and ten bounds it badly. At thirty it is a thirtieth; at a hundred it is a hundredth.
#   THIRTY WAS THE NUMBER THAT LET THE BOUND BE MEASURED, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAID TO EXTEND. This header
#   stated before any rank was drawn that if the curve were still climbing at thirty the draw extends. It is
#   still climbing, and it will not stop: the disagreement between two references built from disjoint halves
#   of the draw falls as the sample size to the power -0.301, where averaging independent draws would give
#   -0.5. That exponent is between-repository heterogeneity rather than sampling noise, so no sample size
#   ends it. About one verdict in ten moves at thirty, all of it among words whose claim sits near zero.
#   A HUNDRED IS A BUDGET, NOT A DERIVED BOUND, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. Every threshold inside a reading
#   here is derived from a null; how much source a project is willing to fetch is not that kind of number.
#   What the measurements settle is the shape of the trade, and three readings of it point at a hundred.
#   One repository's weight falls to a hundredth, an order of magnitude below the tenth that made ten
#   unusable. The words that move are the ones estimated from almost no repositories — `buf` is carried by
#   an effective 4.94 of the thirty — and a hundred takes that to about sixteen, which is where a share
#   stops being one repository's accident. And past it the curve is flat: three hundred repositories buy
#   about two further points of churn for three times the source.
#   WHAT ACTUALLY SETTLES THE CHURN IS NOT SAMPLE SIZE. A word whose claim sits inside the reference's own
#   sampling error has not been shown to stand above chance, and that error is derivable from the split-half
#   measurement above rather than chosen. Reporting it is what makes the near-zero verdicts stop flipping,
#   and it costs no bandwidth at all.
#   EXTENDING A SEEDED DRAW IS NOT RE-ROLLING IT, ONCE THE FRAME IS FIXED. Further rows are the next values
#   from the same stream, so every row already recorded stays exactly as it was — which holds only because
#   the frame no longer moves under it, and is why the upper bound on `pushed` above was worth a re-draw. That is what makes growing a sample
#   different in kind from drawing it again until it looks right. The other two manifests can be grown the
#   same way without invalidating a row.
# Columns, the seeded draw, the exact-count method and the doctrine argument are as reference-corpus.tsv
# states them; only the frame and the predicate differ. The draw is CorpusDrawCommand, which writes both the
# record of every rank and rejection and the rows below.
# Source: THIS PROJECT ran the draw; GitHub states the frame, the licence enumeration and the ranks.
